title: Scaling Mathematical Proof Supervision from Structured Textbooks
task: Structured mathematical supervision from textbooks for proof reasoning
key_results: 380K structured proof-supervision records from 2,118 textbooks; 16.7 percentage point improvement over base model on held-out evaluations
comments: Preserving textbook structure (chapters, propositions, dependencies) appears crucial; curriculum learning signals warrant further investigation.

model_io.model: Language model (base + fine-tuned)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Structured textbook organization improves mathematical reasoning over flattened problem-solution pairs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 16.7pp improvement; curriculum learning and source breadth show positive scaling

title: SteerDistill: Quantizing LLM Agents via Closed-Loop Teacher Steering
task: Quantization-aware distillation for LLM agents with closed-loop steering
key_results: W4A16 quantization within 1 point of BF16; 1.67–2.18pp improvement over baselines; 67% fewer training GPU hours than QeRL
comments: Closed-loop teacher steering elegantly addresses the offline data cold-start problem by iteratively correcting behavioral divergences.

model_io.model: Full-precision teacher + quantized student

hypotheses.hypothesis: Quantized agents fail by ignoring task requirements; closed-loop steering can correct these via iterative guidance
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: SteerDistill recovers performance and produces shorter successful trajectories

title: Incentivizing Self-Learning in Large Language Models via Reinforcement Learning
task: Self-learning from long-form textbooks via RL for domain-adaptive reasoning
key_results: 79.5% proof accuracy (51.5% baseline) on textbook math; 1.7–2.3pp gains on BrowseComp-Plus and CL-bench
comments: RL incentive structure for self-learning is domain-agnostic; textbook navigation as explicit interface is a clever proxy for human study processes.

model_io.model: LLM + BookNavigator interface + RL training

hypotheses.hypothesis: RL incentivizes tightly coupled knowledge acquisition and reasoning from long-form materials better than retrieval-augmented generation
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Self-learning improves in-domain and out-of-domain; transfers to complex long-context tasks

title: Ensemble Routing for Prompt-Adaptive Cost-Aware LLM Inference
task: Prompt-adaptive, cost-aware LLM routing with ensemble selection
key_results: PISA-E achieves 2.09pp (ID) and 2.87pp (OOD) improvement over ensemble baselines; 36–25% cost reduction at selected operating points
comments: Soft cluster memberships + model-specific predictors enable adaptive composition without ensemble-specific training; cost-quality tradeoff adjustment at inference time is valuable.

model_io.model: Soft clustering + model predictors + ensemble router

hypotheses.hypothesis: Prompt-adaptive capability estimation improves both single-model and ensemble routing under ID and OOD conditions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: PISA-E highest macro-average performance; maintains quality while reducing cost

title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
task: Evaluation and RL in AAA game environments (GTA V)
key_results: 70.9% accuracy on GTAVBench-AGI; LoRA RL improves navigation from 15% to 23% with transfer to out-of-domain tasks
comments: Automatic engine-state outcome verification is a significant contribution; aerial navigation and evasion remain hard even for frontier LLMs.

model_io.model: LLM + RL (LoRA) on GTA V environment

hypotheses.hypothesis: Frontier LLMs can complete GTA V tasks at reasonable accuracy but struggle with dynamic tasks like evasion
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 70.9% overall; RL improves navigation and transfers to unseen task categories

title: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading of External Content for AI Agents
task: Token-efficient sparse reading of external content for AI agents
key_results: Up to 92.9% token reduction and 89.0% latency reduction; 97% of settings preserve or improve task quality
comments: Read Intent Protocol + Adaptive Reader Backends + Budgeted Read Gate is a modular, model-agnostic design; 31–43% token reduction on web deep-search is significant.

model_io.model: Reusable reading control layer (SparseRead)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Controlled sparse reading reduces token/latency costs without sacrificing task quality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Up to 92.9% token reduction; 97% settings maintain or improve quality

title: Evolving Infra: Agent-Adaptive LLM Serving at Scale
task: Runtime-adaptive LLM serving for agentic workloads with decoupled prefill-decode
key_results: Up to 4.1x reduction in mean latency and 14x reduction in P95 TTFT over Dynamo on coding/math/computer-use tasks
comments: Decoupling compute allocation from KV cache management is elegant; agent-aware cache eviction via context signals captures domain-specific patterns.

model_io.model: Agent-adaptive serving framework (Evolving Infra)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Agent-aware compute and cache management reduces latency and P95 TTFT vs. coarse workload signals
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 4.1–14x improvements on diverse agent tasks across two large models

title: Where Does Alignment Emerge and What Does It Mean? A Closer Look at the Platonic Representation Hypothesis
task: Investigating representational alignment between vision and language models
key_results: Cross-modal alignment persists for newer models with clean captions; can exceed explicitly-aligned vision-language models but remains below same-modality alignment
comments: Proper baselines for depth/width confounds are essential; caption quality is a critical moderator not highlighted in prior work.

model_io.model: Unimodal vision + language models

hypotheses.hypothesis: Platonic Representation Hypothesis (capability-alignment trend) holds for newer models given sufficiently clean captions
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Trend persists; cross-modal alignment can exceed vision-language models but stays below unimodal alignment

title: Mixed Signals: Weight-Space Programming for EEG and ECG
task: Weight-space programming to write and debug biosignal neural networks (EEG/ECG)
key_results: LLM-written networks match gradient descent with 6× fewer training subjects; surpass hand-crafted EEG pipelines; unable to improve well-trained models
comments: Novel application of weight-space reasoning; limited by inability to recognize task structure from weights alone and scale to larger models.

model_io.model: Claude Opus 5.5 + biosignal model architecture

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLMs can reason about weight values to train biosignal networks more sample-efficiently than gradient descent
hypotheses.result: Confirmed for small networks: 6× fewer subjects; competitive with hand-crafted pipelines; fails on pre-trained models

title: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks
task: Graph-aware optimizer adapting matrix updates to covariance structure of propagated features
key_results: GraphMuon achieves 1.32–2.42× validation-loss time-to-target speedups over AdamW on OGB benchmarks; lower time-to-target in 13/15 configurations
comments: Insight that graph-propagated representations amplify weight updates is elegant; orthogonalization in propagation-metric space is a natural fix.

model_io.model: GraphMuon optimizer for GNNs

hypotheses.hypothesis: Vanilla matrix-aware optimizers suffer from graph-induced update amplification; graph-metric orthogonalization mitigates this
hypotheses.result: Confirmed theoretically and empirically: GraphMuon achieves 1.32–2.42× speedups with competitive performance

title: CogBattery: Human-Referenced Evaluation of Cognitive Task Behavior and Structure in Language Models
task: Evaluating LLM cognitive task behavior against human data from 13 paradigms
key_results: Models reproduce human effect directions but make far more false alarms; most models show weaker confidence calibration than humans; no scale guarantee of human-likeness
comments: Critical insight: matching effect direction ≠ human-like cognition; predefined cognitive groupings show no predictive advantage over random groupings.

model_io.model: 54 open-weight LLMs on 13 cognitive tasks

hypotheses.hypothesis: Larger models converge toward human cognitive behavior patterns
hypotheses.result: Partially rejected: Scale correlates with first dimension but larger ≠ consistently more human-like; effect-direction matching masks different error structures

title: WMIP: A Working-Memory-Inspired Programmable Probe of Cumulative State Tracking in Large Language Models
task: Testing cumulative state tracking in LLMs with working-memory-inspired probes
key_results: 84.9% on single-step but 31.7% on multi-update tracking; >100 updates: <10% accuracy; output protocol substantially changes measured accuracy
comments: Strong single-step arithmetic does not ensure cumulative tracking; protocol effects (write steps, final-line placement) are surprisingly large.

model_io.model: 18 LLMs on working-memory probe (WMIP)

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLMs maintain single-step arithmetic but struggle with cumulative updates without explicit intermediate states
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 31.7% accuracy on core multi-update items; output protocol changes performance by up to 56pp

title: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model
task: Adaptive weight precision during decoding to balance quality and cost
key_results: Entropy-based escalation at 16% budget matches 8-bit quality at 87% of weight bytes; live results inconclusive (p=0.080)
comments: Clever use of entropy as a signal for uncertain steps; limited statistical power on live GSM8K makes conclusions tentative.

model_io.model: Qwen3-0.6B with simulated mixed-precision quantization

hypotheses.hypothesis: Entropy-based escalation from 4-bit to 8-bit at uncertain steps recovers quality with lower total weight bytes than fixed precision
hypotheses.result: Supported in simulation (AUC 0.93 on argmax flips); live GSM8K results inconclusive (McNemar p=0.053–0.080)

title: Interactive Visual Gym: Evaluating Visual Interaction Models with Simulated Users in Interactive Worlds
task: Closed-loop evaluation of visual interaction models in simulated physical task environments
key_results: Gemini 4 Argon completes only 53.4% of tasks; 78.5% human agreement with interaction-quality metric; GRPO closed-loop training improves success and quality
comments: Persona-conditioned user simulation + out-of-plan behaviors add realism; offline replay cannot capture closed-loop effects like assistant response latency.

model_io.model: VLM + simulated task environment + user simulator + GRPO training

hypotheses.hypothesis: Closed-loop evaluation reveals VLM weaknesses missed in offline benchmarks; closed-loop training improves both task success and interaction quality
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 53.4% best performance; offline replay cannot capture latency-induced failures; GRPO improves cooking domain performance

title: CARTBench: Rubric-Based Evaluation of Shopping Advice for Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines
task: Rubric-based evaluation of LLM shopping advice for complex, ambiguous requests with timelines
key_results: 3/10 models exceed 90% on Core criteria; none exceeds 45% on Excellence; understanding-to-execution gap identified across product evidence and unresolved needs
comments: Case-specific rubrics distilled from successful orders are more nuanced than one-size-fits-all criteria; 1,603 product records + temporal metadata add realism.

model_io.model: 7 flagship APIs + 35B+ open-weight models

hypotheses.hypothesis: LLM shopping assistants execute basic recommendations but fail on excellence criteria (nuance, evidence, need resolution)
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: Core ~90%, Excellence <45%; shared failures in product grounding and requirement tracking

title: Bits or permutations? Spending a fixed inference budget on weight precision or on option-order averaging in small local language models
task: Quantization vs. option-reordering averaging trade-off in small local LLMs
key_results: 6-bit weights no accuracy loss vs. fp16; 4-bit + 4 cyclic orders recovers +12.6pp on 0.6B; 6-bit + up to 4 reorderings outperforms 6-bit alone in cost-matched comparisons
comments: First systematic study of quantization-reordering trade-off; machine-independent cost metric (weight bytes × passes) enables fair comparison.

model_io.model: Qwen3-0.6B, Qwen3-1.7B with simulated quantization

hypotheses.hypothesis: In a fixed inference budget, spending on multiple reorderings (4 cyclic orders) beats extra weight precision beyond 6 bits
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 6-bit + up to 4 orders preferred over higher precision; 4-bit + averaging recovers +12.6pp at cost of reorderings

title: PolyRoute: A Twelve-Language and Code-Mixed Benchmark for Typed-Decision Routing, with Baselines and a Leaderboard
task: Multilingual and code-mixed routing classification across 12 languages with typed-decision routing
key_results: Shipped multilingual checkpoint 77.3%; best fine-tune 96.6%; TF-IDF + logistic regression 91.9%; on withheld languages three systems score 77%, 90%, 93%
comments: Code-mixed English-root (85%) nominally beats multilingual (79%, p=0.134); statistical power limited; all texts LLM-generated.

model_io.model: 13 routing systems (English-root, multilingual, fine-tuned variants)
inputs: support messages in 12 languages/9 writing systems

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multilingual checkpoints generalize to withheld languages better than English-root; fine-tuning boosts performance substantially
hypotheses.result: Confirmed: 77–93% on held-out languages; fine-tuning reaches 96.6%; English-root competent on code-mixed but not statistically separable

title: Epigenetic gatekeeping enables genome-scale horizontal gene transfer in eukaryotic cells
task: Establish epigenetic mechanisms enabling stable eukaryotic horizontal gene transfer at genome scale
key_results: Mammalian cells retain >16 Mb algal DNA including intact chromosomes as telomere-linked structures for 95 generations; transferred DNA undergoes progressive methylation and repressive histone modifications; de novo DNA methyltransferase deficiency reduces stable retention
comments: Striking demonstration of epigenetic gatekeeping in foreign genome accommodation; however, functional consequences of retained algal DNA and whether any genes are expressed remains unclear.

model_io.model: Mammalian cell lines with algal cell uptake

hypotheses.hypothesis: De novo DNA methylation gates stable establishment of transferred foreign DNA
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; methyltransferase-deficient cells show reduced stable retention

title: The optogenetic tool ASAP acutely inhibits autophagy
task: Develop optogenetic tool to rapidly inhibit autophagy and identify regulated substrates
key_results: ASAP inhibits autophagy within 5 min; identified nuclear pore complex proteins as tightly regulated autophagy substrates; cytoplasmic nucleoporin complexes accumulate in P bodies upon inhibition
comments: Elegant optogenetic approach enables temporal precision, though the physiological relevance of rapid 5-min inhibition versus sustained autophagy suppression remains to be clarified.

model_io.model: Light-induced proteolytic cleavage system (ASAP)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Nuclear pore complex proteins are selective autophagy substrates
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; identified as tightly regulated autophagy substrates with LC3-interacting regions

title: TMEM192 is a calcineurin-regulated membrane receptor for ubiquitin-independent lysophagy
task: Identify ubiquitin-independent lysophagy receptor and mechanism
key_results: TMEM192 mediates lysophagy independent of ubiquitin; calcineurin dephosphorylates TMEM192 at Ser229 enabling LC3 recruitment; TMEM192 deficiency exacerbates renal injury in hyperuricemic nephropathy model
comments: Discovery of calcineurin-regulated, ubiquitin-independent lysophagy pathway is significant for understanding lysosomal stress responses and has potential therapeutic implications.

model_io.model: Cell culture with lysosomal damage and TMEM192 manipulation
Mouse model of acute hyperuricemic nephropathy

hypotheses.hypothesis: TMEM192 functions as ubiquitin-independent lysophagy receptor
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; lysophagy persists when ubiquitination inhibited or adaptors deleted

hypotheses.hypothesis: Calcineurin regulates TMEM192 to enable autophagosome recruitment
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; dephosphorylation at Ser229 exposes LC3-interacting region

title: Ms4a6d in macrophages accelerated the progression of AAA via modulating SYK/PI3K/CREB/STING signaling induced inflammation and MMPs expression
task: Determine role of Ms4a6d in macrophage-driven abdominal aortic aneurysm progression
key_results: Ms4a6d overexpression increased AAA diameter and macrophage infiltration; establishes SYK/PI3K/CREB/STING signaling axis driving inflammation and MMP expression; genetic and pharmacological interventions confirm hierarchical pathway
comments: Comprehensive in vivo and in vitro validation with sequential pharmacological intervention strengthens mechanistic claims, though the role of Ms4a6d in other cell types remains unaddressed.

model_io.model: ApoE-/- mouse AAA model
RAW264.7 macrophages with Ang II and hypoxia

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ms4a6d regulates hierarchical SYK/PI3K/CREB/STING signaling in macrophages
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; sequential pharmacological blocks demonstrate pathway hierarchy

title: Perphenazine inhibits Toll-like receptor 3-dependent nuclear factor κB activation induced by a double-stranded RNA analogue
task: Identify TLR3-dependent NF-κB pathway inhibitor and mechanism
key_results: Perphenazine inhibits Poly(I:C)-induced NF-κB activation and adhesion molecule expression; binds MICOS complex subunit MIC60; MIC60 silencing inhibits IκBα phosphorylation
comments: MIC60 as a regulator of TLR3/NF-κB signaling is unexpected and suggests mitochondrial organellar contact sites play roles beyond bioenergetics.

model_io.model: Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Perphenazine binds MIC60 to inhibit TLR3-NF-κB signaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; MIC60 silencing recapitulates perphenazine inhibition of IκBα phosphorylation

title: Benzo[a]pyrene induces metabolic alterations and associated effects on cholesterol and vitamin D-related pathways in zebrafish embryos
task: Characterize BaP-induced metabolic alterations and their link to endocrine-metabolic dysfunction in developing embryos
key_results: BaP reduces hatching and survival; induces ROS accumulation; causes metabolic reprogramming in lipid, amino acid, and energy metabolism; alters cyp2r1 and dhcr7 expression suggesting cholesterol and vitamin D pathway disruption
comments: Systems-level NMR metabolomics approach is comprehensive; however, causal linkage between metabolic alterations and developmental abnormalities is correlative rather than mechanistically established.

model_io.model: Zebrafish embryo developmental toxicity model

hypotheses.hypothesis: BaP-induced metabolic reprogramming involves altered cholesterol and vitamin D metabolism
hypotheses.result: Supported; cyp2r1 and dhcr7 expression changes observed

title: Danlou Tablets modulates the HMGCR-mediated MVA pathway, targeting ferroptosis and cholesterol synthesis to combat hepatocellular carcinoma
task: Investigate mechanisms by which Danlou Tablets inhibit hepatocellular carcinoma via HMGCR-mediated pathway
key_results: DLT contains 1003 components; 8 show HMGCR binding by docking; DLT inhibits cholesterol synthesis and promotes ferroptosis in HCC cells; HMGCR overexpression reverses DLT effects on MVA pathway and ferroptosis
comments: Herbal medicine approach with complex multi-component activity makes mechanistic attribution challenging; HMGCR dependence is demonstrated but contribution of individual components remains unclear.

model_io.model: Clinical HCC tissues and in vitro HCC cell models

hypotheses.hypothesis: DLT inhibits HCC by regulating HMGCR-mediated MVA pathway to suppress cholesterol synthesis and promote ferroptosis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; HMGCR overexpression reverses DLT-induced inhibition

title: Isofalcarintriol ameliorates gestational diabetes mellitus-induced β-cell dysfunction by targeting MIF to enhance mitophagy
task: Identify mechanism by which isofalcarintriol ameliorates GDM-induced β-cell dysfunction
key_results: IFT promotes MIF ubiquitination and dissociation from USP7, driving PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy; enhances β-cell antioxidant capacity and reverses HG/PA-induced dysfunction in vitro and in vivo
comments: Natural product targeting MIF-USP7 interaction is interesting, though the specificity of IFT binding and off-target effects in complex biological systems warrant caution.

model_io.model: High-fat diet pregnant mouse model
MIN6 β-cell model with HG/PA treatment

hypotheses.hypothesis: MIF ubiquitination drives PINK1/Parkin mitophagy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; PINK1 knockdown reverses mitophagy promotion by MIF knockdown

hypotheses.hypothesis: IFT targets MIF-USP7 interaction via C224 residue
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; promotes MIF dissociation and ubiquitination

title: Interpreting NADH fluorescence lifetime across timescales
task: Clarify interpretation of NADH fluorescence lifetime measurements across physiological timescales
key_results: NADH lifetime reflects both glycolysis/oxidative respiration balance and temporal dynamics of enzyme expression; slow changes (hours-days) reshape NADH-binding enzyme landscape; rapid metabolite engagement (<1 min) transiently alters apparent lifetime
comments: Perspective highlights critical interpretive framework for a widely-used technique; emphasizes need for experimental design rigor but lacks quantitative guidelines for timescale-dependent measurement validity.

title: StrataChip: a microphysiological system to capture dynamic keratinocyte fate and mechanical transitions during human epidermal morphogenesis
task: Develop microphysiological system to interrogate keratinocyte differentiation and mechanical transitions during epidermal morphogenesis
key_results: StrataChip recapitulates human epidermis with basal, spinous, and granular layers; single-cell RNA-seq identifies transcriptionally distinct basal and spinous subpopulations with transitional states; live imaging captures basal cell delamination and asymmetric division
comments: Excellent integration of tissue engineering, live-cell imaging, and single-cell sequencing; however, the mechanical properties are inferred from morphology rather than directly measured.

model_io.model: StrataChip microphysiological system

hypotheses.hypothesis: StrataChip recapitulates key architectural and molecular features of human epidermis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; canonical differentiation markers and layer organization observed

title: Intrinsic and acquired transcriptional programs shape heterogeneous tumor cell responses to PARP, Akt, and CDK4/6 inhibitors
task: Dissect intrinsic vs. acquired transcriptional programs driving heterogeneous TNBC response to targeted therapies
key_results: Non-genetic heterogeneity drives response to PARP, Akt, and CDK4/6 inhibitors; intrinsic transcriptomic state and persistent treatment-induced changes both predict survival in therapy-tolerant subpopulations
comments: ClonMapper tracking elegantly separates pre-treatment and adaptive programs, but functional validation of identified transcriptional drivers and translational applicability require follow-up.

model_io.model: ClonMapper cell barcoding with scRNA-seq

hypotheses.hypothesis: Intrinsic and acquired transcriptional programs independently predict therapy resistance
hypotheses.result: Survival modeled as combination of pre-treatment transcriptomic state and persistent drug-induced expression changes; non-genetic heterogeneity drives therapeutic response

title: PANGEA: an integrated cell atlas across diverse biological contexts enables systematic profiling of multicellular responses in human diseases
task: Integrate multi-source single-cell data to map disease-associated multicellular responses across tissues
key_results: PANGEA integrates 46.5 million cells from 160 diseases across 48 organs; identifies core disease archetypes and reveals spatial features associated with immunotherapy response
comments: Large-scale atlas construction from public repositories is valuable but phenotypic validation of disease archetypes and causal mechanisms remain unexplored.

model_io.model: PANGEA hierarchical cell classification framework
inputs: 12.6 million single-cell transcriptomes from public repositories

hypotheses.hypothesis: Core multicellular response archetypes are conserved across organs in human diseases
hypotheses.result: Identified recurrent disease archetypes; validated through spatial transcriptomics immune-response associations

title: Effective regulatory relationships between genes differ from direct transcription factor-target interactions, and exhibit a distinct statistical signature
task: Distinguish effective regulatory relationships from direct transcription factor-target interactions
key_results: Effective regulators form small network with distinct statistical signature; lack of statistical association between TF activity and direct targets; effective networks exhibit greater clustering than canonical TF networks
comments: Computational and perturbation-based approach clarifies regulatory network topology, but mechanistic basis of indirect regulation and tissue-specificity warrant further investigation.

model_io.model: Gene regulatory network model with perturbation validation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Effective regulatory relationships exhibit distinct statistical properties compared to direct TF-target interactions
hypotheses.result: Effective regulators form small clustering-enriched networks with diffuse distribution throughout transcriptional network; display measurable statistical signature

title: A privacy preserving federated learning framework for rice leaf disease classification and severity estimation using indian field data
task: Enable privacy-preserving federated learning for rice leaf disease classification with heterogeneous distributed data
key_results: Achieves 95.49% disease classification accuracy and 94.57% severity estimation in five-client federated setup; maintains >91% and >92% accuracy respectively with increased client participation
comments: Federated framework addresses practical agricultural deployment challenges, but real-world field validation and comparison to centralized models across diverse farming regions remain necessary.

model_io.model: ResNet-18 + Convolutional Block Attention Module with model-contrastive federated learning
inputs: Rice leaf images from heterogeneous Indian agricultural regions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Model-contrastive federated learning mitigates client drift under non-IID data distribution
hypotheses.result: Classification accuracy 95.49%, severity accuracy 94.57% in five-client setup; stable >91% and >92% performance with increased clients

title: Positional encoding cross-attention ResNet50 framework for lung cancer classification across CT and histopathological imaging modalities
task: Classify lung cancer from CT and histopathology using positional encoding cross-attention ResNet50
key_results: Framework integrates shallow structural and deep semantic features through cross-attention; improves classification performance across CT and histopathological imaging modalities with spatial information preservation
comments: Intra-modality attention mechanism shows promise, but external validation across diverse patient populations and prospective clinical deployment remain essential before therapeutic guidance.

model_io.model: Positional Encoding Cross-Attention ResNet50 with clinical decision-support module
inputs: Chest CT scans and histopathological images

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cross-attention between shallow structural and deep semantic features enhances lung cancer classification
hypotheses.result: Attention-enhanced architecture improves performance by selectively emphasizing diagnostically relevant regions across imaging modalities

title: UltraSAM-based left ventricular analysis with local–global feature fusion for echocardiographic cardiac disease classification
task: Classify cardiac disease from echocardiography using hybrid deep learning with local-global feature fusion
key_results: Achieves 94.7% accuracy for myocardial infarction detection (93% sensitivity, 97% specificity) on HMC-QU dataset; generalizes to 90.3% binary and 81.4% multi-class on CardiacNet dataset
comments: Hybrid framework combining region-specific and global features shows promise, but clinical deployment requires prospective validation and comparison to expert cardiologist performance.

model_io.model: Hybrid deep learning: UltraSAM segmentation + Swin Transformer + LSTM classification

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fusion of local ventricular features and global cardiac frame representations improves disease classification
hypotheses.result: 94.7% accuracy MI detection; 90.3% binary and 81.4% multi-class accuracy on external dataset demonstrates effective multi-scale feature integration

title: Comprehensive comparative genomics of camelids identifies positive selection, structural variants, and gene losses driving desert adaptation
task: Identify genomic signatures of desert adaptation in camelids through comparative genomics
key_results: Detected CYP gene family reorganization (CYP2J expansion, CYP4F contraction); 47 positively selected genes including HACD3 with ultraconserved D270N substitution; 10 pseudogenized genes (CES3, CPA3, PLA2G2F, TAS2R16)
comments: Comprehensive comparative analysis provides strong correlative evidence, but most inferred adaptive mechanisms remain untested; functional validation in camelids is critical and authors acknowledge current lack of mechanistic proof.

model_io.model: Comparative genomics pipeline: OrthoFinder + branch-site analysis + copy-number variation detection + pseudogene screening
inputs: 11 mammalian genomes (3 Old World camels, 4 New World camels, pig, cattle, human, mouse)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Lineage-specific copy-number changes, positive selection, and gene loss drive desert adaptation in camelids
hypotheses.result: CYP gene reorganization, HACD3 positive selection, and pseudogenization of lipid-metabolism genes detected; TAS2R16 loss experimentally confirmed but adaptive significance remains hypothetical

title: Assessment of interkingdom TIR domain interactions using a modular yeast tripartite split-GFP system
task: Develop modular yeast system to systematically detect interkingdom TIR domain protein-protein interactions
key_results: ytpGFP successfully detected known and previously unknown TIR-TIR interactions; human MyD88, TIRAP, TRAM, TRIF interact with bacterial BtpA and BtpB with differential efficiency; N-terminal extensions modulate interaction capacity
comments: Yeast-based system provides high-throughput screening capability, but recapitulation of native signaling context and in vivo relevance of detected interactions require validation.

model_io.model: Yeast tripartite split-GFP (ytpGFP) system coupled to MoClo modular cloning
inputs: TIR domain-containing proteins (bacterial BtpA, BtpB; human myddosome and triffosome adaptors)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bacterial TIR domains interact with human innate immune adaptors with differential efficiency dependent on N-terminal extensions
hypotheses.result: Detected heterotypic interactions between BtpA/BtpB and MyD88/TIRAP/TRAM/TRIF; N-terminal regions limit TIR-TIR interaction capacity

title: NeuroMemory-DiffNet: a reference-guided memory framework for brain tumor segmentation and classification
task: Segment and classify brain tumors using reference-guided difference learning with anatomical priors
key_results: Achieves 98.70% multi-class classification accuracy, 96.31% Dice similarity coefficient for segmentation on BraTS 2023; interpretable framework highlights structural deviations from healthy anatomy
comments: Reference-guided approach enhances interpretability, but external validation and clinical integration require prospective studies to confirm diagnostic utility.

model_io.model: NeuroMemory-DiffNet: NAPM + Reference-Guided Difference Learning + Healthy-Reference Reconstruction

hypotheses.hypothesis: Reference-guided estimation of deviations from healthy anatomy improves tumor classification and segmentation with enhanced interpretability
hypotheses.result: 98.70% classification accuracy with 98.70% F1-score; 96.31% DSC segmentation achieves competitive benchmark performance with anatomical consistency constraints

title: Comprehensive molecular and clinical analysis of human electron transfer flavoprotein variants in multiple Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency
task: Characterize pathogenic mechanisms of hETF variants in Multiple Acyl-CoA Dehydrogenase Deficiency through integrated molecular and clinical analysis
key_results: Interface SNPs (βE165K, αN259S, αN259D) disrupt inter-subunit interactions driving open conformation with 15% ΔSASA FAD cofactor exposure; clinical classification identifies rs1441796075 as Likely Pathogenic, two variants remain VUS; consensus destabilization predictions for αN259S (3/3 methods) and βE165K (2/3 methods)
comments: Integrated computational-clinical approach elegantly links structure to pathology, but predicted therapeutic intervention (interface stabilizers) and functional consequences of gene losses remain experimental hypotheses requiring preclinical validation.

model_io.model: Structure-function-disease pipeline: homology modeling + stability predictions (DynaMut, mCSM, DUET) + SAXS analysis + ACMG/AMP clinical classification

hypotheses.hypothesis: Interface-destabilizing variants promote open conformation and FAD vulnerability to pathogenic oxidation
hypotheses.result: All three SNPs disrupt inter-subunit interactions increasing ΔSASA >15%; small-molecule interface stabilizers proposed as testable therapeutic strategy

title: A hypothesis-generating multi-resolution post-GWAS analysis of context-dependent regulatory signals in migraine
task: Identify context-dependent regulatory signals and effector genes in migraine through multi-resolution post-GWAS analysis
key_results: Single-cell TWAS identified 39 genes including LRP1 (positive in effector-memory CD4+ T cells), PTBP2/MRPS21/TAGLN3 (negative in immune cells); broad eQTL/sQTL enrichment across tissues; PTBP2 has broadest multi-method support; LRP1 context-dependent; TAGLN3 exploratory
comments: Comprehensive integrative analysis generates testable regulatory hypotheses, but acknowledged caution that associations do not establish causal genes, tissues, or mechanisms—experimental validation essential.

model_io.model: Multi-method post-GWAS pipeline: gene-set/QTL enrichment, single-cell/bulk TWAS, PoPS, FOCUS, colocalization, spatial/regulatory annotations
inputs: GWAS summary statistics (FinnGen, UK Biobank, Million Veteran Program; 84,123 cases, 1,213,483 controls)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Migraine-associated loci regulate disease through context-dependent mechanisms in immune and vascular tissues
hypotheses.result: LRP1 positive in effector-memory CD4+ T cells; PTBP2 broadly negative across immune cells; findings prioritize regulatory hypotheses but do not establish causality

title: Applying ranked set sampling to Gaussian mixture models of Glasgow Coma Scale scores in intracerebral hemorrhage
task: Enhance component separability in mixture models of clinical severity scales using ranked set sampling
key_results: Ranked set sampling reduced component overlap substantially compared to simple random sampling while maintaining three-component structure; concentrated mixture components without increasing model complexity
comments: Practical methodological contribution for heterogeneous medical data, but limited to single clinical outcome; broader applicability across severity scales warrants exploration.

model_io.model: Gaussian mixture model with ranked set sampling vs. simple random sampling
inputs: Glasgow Coma Scale scores (N=504 ICH patients)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Ranked set sampling improves component separability in mixture models without increasing complexity
hypotheses.result: Retrospective RSS-based subsampling yielded more concentrated components and substantially reduced overlap between adjacent components compared to SRS

title: DeepTNR: predicting tumor drug sensitivity from spatial transcriptomics with deep graph contrastive and transfer learning
task: Predict tumor drug sensitivity incorporating spatial organization and tumor-stroma interactions

hypotheses.hypothesis: High-pressure uranium polyhydrides (UH7, UH8) decompose to lower hydrides upon decompression
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; hcp-UH7 decomposes to hcp-UH5 below 27 GPa; U4H15 is recoverable to ambient pressure

title: Memristors
task: Comprehensive review of memristor physics, applications, and research ecosystem development
key_results: Memristors exhibit diverse dynamics beyond RRAM (ionic migration, electrochemical reactions, phase evolution); applications span non-volatile memory, in-memory computing, neuromorphic systems; standardization and reproducibility frameworks identified as critical gaps
comments: This Primer synthesizes the field methodologically and highlights systemic needs (standardized reporting, benchmarking) that are as important as individual device advances for sustained progress.

model_io.model: memristor device (various material platforms and mechanisms)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Memristor switching behavior is governed by internal physical-state evolution (ionic migration, phase change, electrochemistry)
hypotheses.result: Confirmed across diverse material platforms; dynamics determine suitability for different applications
